1. Compromise affidavit filed by the counsel for the opposite party no.2, is taken on record.
2. Heard counsel for the applicants, Sri Sunil Kumar Misra, learned counsel for the opposite party no.2 and Sri Neeraj Kumar Sharma, learned A.G.A. for the State.

3. The present 482 Cr.P.C. application has been filed with the prayer to quash the entire proceedings of Case No. 5609 of 2023 (State Vs. Puneet and others), arising out of Case Crime No. 296 of 2022,
under Sections 498A, 323, 504 IPC and Section 3/4 Dowry Prohibition Act, Police Station- Brahmpuri, District Meerut, pending in the Court of Addl. Civil Judge (Jr. Div.)/Judicial Magistrate,

sentences.text:
4. Learned counsel for the applicants submits that:-
(i) the dispute arises out of matrimonial discord between the applicant no. 1 and the opposite party no. 2. The applicants no. 2 to 4 are the family members of the applicant no.1.

It is further stated that pursuant to the order dated 28.08.2023 passed by this Court in Application U/s 482 Cr.P.C. No. 29344 of 2023, the parties appeared and the court concerned verified the aforesaid compromise vide order dated 20.10.2023.
Copy of the order dated 20.10.2023 is annexed as Annexure-11 to the affidavit.

6. It is submitted by the learned counsel for the applicants that if the criminal prosecution is allowed to proceed it may create further complication in the otherwise normal relationship that is arising between the hitherto bitterly estranged couple and their families.
7. Learned counsel for the opposite party no. 2 does not dispute the submissions advanced by the counsel for the applicants or the correctness of the documents relied upon by him.

8. In view of the fact that the dispute appears to be purely of a personal nature being a matrimonial dispute that has been mutually settled between the parties, to their satisfaction, no useful purpose would be served in allowing such a prosecution to proceed any further.

9. Thus, in view of the well settled principles of law as laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in B.S.
Joshi v. State of Haryana, 2003(4) SCC 675, as well as Nikhil Merchant v. Central Bureau of Investigation and another, J.T., 2008 (9) SC 192, the proceedings of the aforesaid case are hereby set aside.
